newsitem.title: ZAIRE: U.N. team to help refugees near Zairean city.
newsitem.headline: U.N. team to help refugees near Zairean city.

text.p: U.N. aid workers arrived in the northeastern Zairean capital of Kisangani on Wednesday to help tens of thousands of refugees stranded on the banks of the Zaire river.

A spokeswoman for the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) said a WFP plane loaded with 35 tonnes of food also landed in Kisangani -- taken at the weekend by rebels seeking to topple President Mobutu Sese Seko -- to help feed 40,000 Zaireans displaced by civil war.

Some 70,000 Rwandan refugees are camped on the Zaire river's east bank at Ubundu, 100 km (60 miles) south of Kisangani, while 30,000 more have crossed to the western bank, the U.N. refugee agency said.
"The condition of the refugees there is desperate with many, many people drowning as they try to cross the river," said Paul Stromberg, spokesman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).
Boatmen plying narrow canoes across the river at Kisangani said they had seen 28 bodies floating downstream since Monday.
Staff from UNHCR, WFP, the U.N. children's fund (UNICEF) and the agency Medecins sans Frontieres (MSF-Doctors Without Borders (MSF) arrived by air from the border town of Goma on Wednesday.
"We hope to overfly the area of Ubundu and we hope to begin helping as quickly as possible," said Stromberg, adding that food for the refugees at Ubundu was scheduled to run out on Wednesday.
Zairean rebels who seized Kisangani on Saturday declared a temporary ceasefire around the city to allow aid agencies in and people who fled to return and have also said they would not attack Ubundu.

WFP spokeswoman Michele Quintaglie said an plane loaded with 35 tonnes of food arrived in Kisangani from Mwanza, Tanzania, after turning back when it was ordered by radio to land in the rebel city of Goma.
She said it later received permission to fly direct to the northeastern capital and the food would be distributed among the 40,000 Zaireans who had sought refuge there after fleeing their homes.

The Rwandan refugees at Ubundu who have been fleeing the rebel advances that started in October left Rwanda in 1994 fearing reprisals for the genocide of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus.
U.N. aid workers were evacuated from Kisangani last Friday before it fell to the rebels.
Quintaglie said rebels told Kisangani's residents they had two days to return looted aid agency food and since Tuesday sacks of food were left on roadsides in the city for aid workers to collect.
"It's pretty incredible. Once it has been looted we don't normally get it back," she said.
